name: Rajiv Gandhi
summary: Gandhi advocated technological modernisation, selective economic liberalisation, rural development and stronger local democracy. He promoted nuclear disarmament and nonalignment while authorising regional military interventions; his secular commitments were complicated by concessions to religious personal law.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass from the five volumes of Selected Speeches and Writings (1984-1989), the 1987 budget speech and a scholarly chapter. Themes searched by keyword: economy (public and private sector, licensing, foreign investment, land reform, unions, prices, taxes, subsidies), government (panchayats, decentralisation, electoral reform, anti-defection, judiciary, press, secession), society (secularism, personal laws, women, caste, language), world (nuclear disarmament, UN, non-alignment, Palestine, South Africa, debt, aid, intervention), ecology and technology. Not found: statements on abortion, same-sex questions, the death penalty, drugs, guns, healthcare as a universal entitlement, immigration, conscription or euthanasia. Answers about what his government did (Sri Lanka, Maldives, Shah Bano law) rest on his own speeches defending them.
